claim: Aire-sur-l'Adour is about 14 km / 16 minutes by car from Eugénie-les-Bains.
quote: Eugénie-les-Bains - Aire-sur-l'Adour driving directions - journey, distance, time and costs – ViaMichelin

claim: The Église Sainte-Quitterie in Aire-sur-l'Adour is a UNESCO-listed stop on the Santiago de Compostela routes, with a Romanesque crypt holding the 4th-century white-marble sarcophagus of Saint Quitterie.
quote: Inscrite au Patrimoine Mondial de l'UNESCO au titre des Chemins de Saint-Jacques de Compostelle… La crypte abrite le sarcophage de Sainte-Quitterie, en marbre blanc de Saint-Béat, datant du milieu du IVe siècle.

claim: Sainte-Quitterie was the first monument classified in the Landes department (1840) and combines a 13th–14th-century Gothic nave with an 11th–12th-century chancel; crypt restored 2018.
quote: L'église a été classée monument historique en 1840, premier monument classé du département des Landes.

claim: Free 45-minute guided visits of Sainte-Quitterie run July 1–Sept 14 (Mon 4–5 pm, Tue–Fri 10–11 am & 4–5 pm, Sat 10–11 am & 3–4 pm); off-season by appointment.
quote: Du 1er juillet au 14 septembre : Visites le lundi à 16h et 17h, du mardi au vendredi à 10h, 11h, 16h et 17h, le samedi à 10h, 11h, 15h et 16h.

claim: Geaune lies about 8 km / 9 minutes south-east of Eugénie-les-Bains.
quote: Eugénie-les-Bains - Geaune : trajet, distance, durée et coûts – ViaMichelin

claim: Geaune is a 1318 English bastide founded by Edward II's Genoese seneschal Antonio de Pessagne, named after Genoa, with a 25-block grid, arcaded square, Augustinian tower, and 15th-century bell tower.
quote: Geaune is a typical bastide city… founded in 1318 by Edward II of England… named after Genoa, the hometown of its founder, the seneschal Antonio de Pessagne.

claim: Geaune is the headquarters of the Cave des Vignerons du Tursan and pairs its bastide walk with AOC Tursan wine tasting.
quote: Geaune est aujourd'hui le siège de la Cave des Vignerons de Tursan et le centre du petit vignoble du Tursan.

claim: Pimbo is the oldest bastide of the Landes, founded by paréage in 1268 between the abbot of Pimbo and a seneschal of the English King Henry III.
quote: Pimbo est la plus ancienne bastide des Landes… fondée en 1268 par un contrat de paréage entre l'abbé de Pimbo et un sénéchal de Gascogne agissant pour le roi d'Angleterre Henri III.

claim: Pimbo's collégiale Saint-Barthélemy (foundation attributed to Charlemagne, 778) is a 12th-century Romanesque church with three naves and three apses on the Via Podiensis to Compostela, and its Jardins du Curé offer a Pyrenees view.
quote: Pimbo, plus ancienne bastide des Landes… la collégiale Saint-Barthélemy dont la fondation est attribuée à Charlemagne en 778.

claim: Pimbo is approximately 13 km from Eugénie-les-Bains by road.
quote: Pimbo is 13.4 km from Eugénie-les-Bains.

claim: Saint-Sever's Benedictine abbey, founded c. late 10th c. by Duke William Sanche of Gascony and UNESCO-listed for the Compostela routes, preserves a rare seven-staggered-apses choir, 77 capitals and a Romanesque tympanum.
quote: Une abbaye-mère qui a conservé un chœur exceptionnel à 7 absides échelonnées du XIème siècle. 77 chapiteaux et un tympan roman ornent l'édifice.

claim: Saint-Sever's cloister Treasure Room displays liturgical objects and a facsimile of the 11th-century illuminated Beatus (the original is at the BnF in Paris); open through Dec 31, 2026.
quote: Salle du trésor de l'abbaye et Beatus de Saint-Sever… une copie en fac-similé du Beatus de Saint-Sever.

claim: Saint-Sever is about 26 km / 29 minutes by car from Eugénie-les-Bains.
quote: Eugénie-les-Bains to Saint-Sever: The drive takes 29 minutes for a distance of 26 kilometers.

claim: In Hagetmau the 12th-century crypt of Saint-Girons — all that survives of the abbey above town — preserves four marble columns and fourteen Romanesque capitals classified as Historic Monuments.
quote: Quatre colonnes de marbre entourent le sol légèrement surélevé… quatorze chapiteaux romans classés Monuments Historiques.

claim: The Hagetmau crypt was a pilgrim stop on the Compostela route; descent is by two lateral staircases in the wall and explanatory leaflets are provided in four languages.
quote: You access the crypt by two lateral staircases built into the thickness of the walls. Details and explanations of each capital are available at the crypt entrance on pamphlets in 4 languages.

claim: Grenade-sur-l'Adour, a 1322 bastide, retains a vast arcaded central square with 14th–15th-century houses; the tourist office provides a six-panel walking tour with booklet.
quote: Bastide fondée en 1322… autour de sa vaste place centrale, bordée d'arcades, témoin de son passé de place forte commerciale et marchande.

claim: Grenade-sur-l'Adour's 15th-century Gothic Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul church (listed historic monument) gained its twin-tower façade in 1833.
quote: L'église Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul, édifice gothique du XVe siècle classé au titre des Monuments historiques, dont la façade à deux tours fut ajoutée en 1833.

claim: Grenade-sur-l'Adour is about 14 km / 16 minutes north of Eugénie-les-Bains by road.
quote: Eugénie-les-Bains to Grenade-sur-l'Adour: The journey takes 16 minutes for a distance of 14.1 kilometres.

claim: Labastide-d'Armagnac, founded 1291 by Count Bernard VI of Armagnac and the King of England, is a Petite Cité de Caractère whose Place Royale — half-timbered arcaded houses around a square — reputedly inspired Henri IV's Place des Vosges in Paris.
quote: Labastide d'Armagnac… une des plus belles bastides du Sud-Ouest… la place Royale aurait inspiré Henri IV pour la place des Vosges à Paris.

claim: Just outside Labastide-d'Armagnac, the Chapelle Notre-Dame-des-Cyclistes is the national sanctuary of cycling (consecrated 1959) and a museum displaying 700+ donated jerseys including Tour de France winners.
quote: Sanctuaire Notre-Dame-des-Cyclistes le 18 mai 1959… musée consacré au cyclisme et aux cyclistes.

claim: Labastide-d'Armagnac is roughly 43 km / 47 minutes from Eugénie-les-Bains — beyond the 30 km radius but a feasible half-day outing.
quote: Distance entre Eugénie-les-Bains et Labastide-d'Armagnac… 43 km, 47 minutes.

claim: Château de Bachen (Duhort-Bachen) is Michel & Christine Guérard's own vineyard since 1983, with first vintage 1987, visitable by appointment only Monday-Friday at 10:00 and 15:00 (closed public holidays), bookings via reservation@lespreseugenie.com.
quote: Visits are by appointment only, Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays), at 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM. Reserve via email at reservation@lespreseugenie.com.

claim: Cave des Vignerons de Tursan in Geaune is about 15 minutes from Eugénie-les-Bains, open Mon-Fri 9-12 / 14-17:30, Sat 9-12:30 (extended Jul-Sept), with guided tour + 5-wine tasting on Tuesdays April-August at 14:30 (plus 10:00 in Jul-Aug) for €5/person, ~90 min, advance reservation required.
quote: Tours available Tuesdays April-August at 2:30pm (plus 10am July-August). The experience includes 'discovering history, exploring the cave and chai' with 'five wines tasted' during roughly 90-minute visits. Cost: €5 per person (18+)... Distance from Eugénie-les-Bains: Approximately 15 minutes away

claim: Cave des Vignerons de Tursan is a 1958 cooperative grouping ~60 growers across 500 hectares producing AOP Tursan red/rosé/white plus IGP Landes wines, located at 30 rue Saint-Jean, 40320 Geaune, with bottles €4.60–€7.65 and curated wine boxes from €35.40.
quote: Founded in 1958, this cooperative winery brings together approximately 60 wine-growers managing 500 hectares of vineyards... Individual wine prices range from €4.60 to €7.65 per bottle (sold in 6-bottle cases). Curated wine boxes are available starting at €35.40.

claim: Geaune sits roughly 6.2 km as the crow flies (about 8 km / 8–9 min by road) from Eugénie-les-Bains, making the Tursan AOC heartland the closest wine cluster to Les Prés d'Eugénie.
quote: The distance to travel from Geaune to Eugénie-les-Bains is 7.7 km for a total duration of approximately 8 minutes... the distance between Geaune and Eugénie-les-Bains is 6.2 km as the crow flies.

claim: Vignoble Dulucq — Château de Perchade is a family-run Tursan estate at 910 route des Pyrénées, 40320 Payros-Cazautets, open year-round by appointment with free tastings of white/rosé/red and sweet Tursan wines, set on a south-facing clay-limestone slope facing the Pyrenees.
quote: Address: 910 route des Pyrénées, 40320 Payros-Cazautets... Visit Hours: 'All year 2026' with visits 'by appointment'... Prices: Free of charge... A south-facing vineyard overlooking the Pyrenees on clay-limestone soil, characterized by wild orchids.

claim: Château Garreau in Labastide-d'Armagnac hosts the Écomusée de l'Armagnac on an 82-hectare estate combining a 17th-c. Musée du Vigneron, an alembic museum with 10+ stills, an underground cellar unique in Armagnac, botanical/pond trails, and a guided Floc de Gascogne + Armagnac tasting at the end of the visit.
quote: Ecomuseum of Armagnac... Vigneron Museum – Houses over 1,000 traditional tools in a 17th-century Gascon barn... Alambics Museum – Features eleven different distillery apparatus... 'A tasting will be offered at the conclusion of the Ecomuseum visit'... distillery operates November-December

claim: Château Garreau Écomusée pricing in 2026: 'Vigneron' visit €6, 'Prince' visit €12, family pass €14 (2 adults + up to 3 children), Écomusée admission €4.50 adult; the site won the 2025 Œnotourism Trophy.
quote: The Winemaker's visit costs €6, the Prince's visit costs €12, and the family rate is €14 (for 2 adults and up to 3 children). Additionally, admission to the Armagnac Ecomuseum is €4.50 for adults... won the Oenotourism Trophies 2025.

claim: Domaine Départemental d'Ognoas (1043 route d'Ognoas, 40190 Arthez-d'Armagnac) — property of the Landes département — opens Tue-Fri with afternoon Monday slots; May-Sept 10-12 / 14-18, Oct-Apr 9-12 / 14-17, tastings €2–€5 covering vintage bas-armagnacs and Floc de Gascogne plus visit of the century-old still.
quote: January-April & October-December: Tuesday-Friday 9am-12pm, 2-5pm; Monday 2-5pm; May-September: Tuesday-Friday 10am-12pm, 2-6pm; Monday 2-6pm... Tastings range from €2-€5... vintage bas-armagnacs, its flocs de Gascogne (local fortified wine), aging cellars and its two century old still.

claim: Domaine d'Ognoas spans 565 hectares of forest, vines and meadows with 7 centuries of history and holds the oldest functioning still in Gascogne (1804, listed Monument Historique); guided tours run at 15:00 Oct-Apr and at 10:00 + 15:00 May-Sept, with escape games and Terra Aventura geocaching also on site.
quote: The domain spans 565 hectares and covers 7 centuries of history, featuring its cellars and the presentation of the oldest functioning still in Gascogne from 1804, which is registered as a historic monument... From October 1st to April 30th, guided visits are available at 3pm, and from May 2nd to September 30th, guided visits are available at 10am and 3pm.

claim: Arthez-d'Armagnac (Domaine d'Ognoas) lies about 24 km from Eugénie-les-Bains, comfortably inside the 30 km radius and noticeably closer than Labastide-d'Armagnac.
quote: Eugénie-les-Bains is situated at 24 km from Arthez-d'Armagnac.

claim: Aire-sur-l'Adour holds its weekly market on Tuesdays AND Saturdays, 8h00–12h30, under Les Halles on Place du Commerce, with about 50 vendors covering bakers, butchers, fishmongers, produce, cheese and wines.
quote: Le marché alimentaire d'Aire sur l'Adour est ouvert les mardis et samedis toute l'année, de 08h00 à 12h30 ... Une cinquantaine de commerçants ... boulangers, bouchers, poissonniers, maraîchers

claim: Saint-Sever's Saturday morning market on Place et Rue du Tribunal features cheesemongers, charcutiers, butchers, fishmongers, pastry shops plus small farm producers selling foie gras, duck, poultry, cheeses, pork and honey.
quote: dans les halles et alentour : fromagers, charcutiers, bouchers, poissonniers, pâtissiers, et de petits producteurs fermiers de foie gras et canard, volailles, primeurs, fromages, porc et miel

claim: From October to April, marchés au gras (fat markets) are essential rendezvous around the Adour valley and Chalosse, the historical foie gras stronghold, with Amou, Geaune, Hagetmau and Saint-Sever hosting open-air duck farms and producer visits.
quote: D'octobre à avril, les marchés au gras dans les Landes sont des rendez-vous incontournables ... autour d'Amou, Geaune, Hagetmau et Saint-Sever, les producteurs sont heureux de faire découvrir aux visiteurs leur élevage de canards

claim: Hagetmau holds its traditional market every Wednesday and Saturday from 8h to 13h on Place Charles De Gaulle, with regional specialties and a summer evening Marché des Producteurs de Pays.
quote: Tous les mercredis et samedis de 8h à 13h ... Place Charles De Gaulle

claim: Grenade-sur-l'Adour hosts producer markets on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday mornings (9h–12h), with Saturday adding takeaway food and Wednesday adding textiles; Le Vignau also runs a Wednesday producer market.
quote: Monday morning (9am-12pm): Producer markets; Wednesday morning (9am-12pm): Producer and textile markets; Saturday morning (9am-12pm): Producer markets and takeaway food

claim: Maison Dubernet, founded 1864 in Saint-Sever, makes hand-crafted foie gras, terrines and confits from IGP Sud-Ouest ducks sourced from a small group of Saint-Sever breeders, with a factory shop open Mon–Thu 8–12 / 14–17 and Fri 8–15, and a first-Friday-of-the-month open house with 15–20% off.
quote: Maison Dubernet, founded in 1864 in the heart of the Landes ... factory shop in Saint-Sever is open Monday to Thursday from 8am to 12pm and 2pm to 5pm ... On the first Friday of each month, there are open houses with an average 15 to 20% discount

claim: Maison Lafitte's Montaut boutique at 455 route du Béarn sits on the production site and opens Mon–Fri 8h–12h30 / 13h30–17h (closed weekends), sourcing ducks from small Landes farms within a 40 km radius fed non-GMO whole grain corn.
quote: 455 route du Béarn, 40500 Montaut ... Monday-Friday: 8:00 AM - 12:30 PM & 1:30 PM - 5:00 PM ... ducks come from small agricultural operations in the Landes within a 40 km radius

claim: Maison Lafitte (Montaut) has worked since 1920 exclusively with ~80 local farms within a 40 km radius and is 100% Label Rouge and IGP Sud-Ouest, with Mulard ducks raised at least 102 days outdoors and fattened on whole grain corn.
quote: 100% certifié Label Rouge et IGP Sud-Ouest ... canard gras élevé pendant minimum 102 jours et gavé au maïs grain entier ... petites exploitations agricoles des Landes situées à moins de 40 km

claim: Ferme Parlariou at Gamarde-les-Bains offers afternoon farm visits by appointment showing the gavage and outdoor duck rearing, plus Blonde d'Aquitaine cattle, with on-site sale of foie gras, confits, pâtés and beef.
quote: Gamarde-les-Bains, 491 route de Mouréou (2 km from Montfort-en-Chalosse) ... ducks, cattle (Blonde d'Aquitaine breed) ... Duck products including fresh fattened ducks, foie gras, preserved items, pâtés, sausages

claim: Parlariou afternoon farm tours are by phone appointment, weather-permitting, at 6€ per adult and 3€ per child (5–15), ending with a free tasting of the producer's foie gras and beef-veal preparations.
quote: sur rendez-vous par téléphone et selon les conditions météo, les après-midi, pour un tarif de 6 € par adulte et 3 € par enfant ... Un moment de dégustation vous sera offert à l'issue de la visite

claim: Geaune is a 1318 bastide whose cooperative wine cellars welcome visitors April–October to introduce Tursan winemaking, in a region also known for Samadet faïence pottery.
quote: Geaune is a bastide of great character created in 1318 ... cooperative wine cellars welcome visitors from April to October and introduce visitors to the art of Tursan winemaking

claim: The Musée départemental de la Faïence et des Arts de la table at Samadet preserves the legacy of the 1732 royal pottery manufactory with over 300 decorated pieces and contemporary ceramics in the adjoining Maison de la Céramique.
quote: manufacture royale de faïence ... établie dans le petit village de Samadet en 1732 ... Plus de 300 pièces de faïence de Samadet

claim: Saint-Sever's En Direct de nos Producteurs boutique aggregates Landes producers (Sarrade, Delpeyrat partners) selling foie gras, magret, confit, prepared dishes, Label Rouge or organic poultry, smoked salmon, Bayonne ham and Pyrenean pork with full traceability.
quote: spécialités du sud-ouest ... canards (foie gras, magret, confit, plats cuisinés et pâtés gourmands), volailles Label Rouge ou bio des Landes, saumon fumé, jambon de Bayonne et porc des Pyrénées

claim: The IGP Canard à Foie Gras du Sud-Ouest covers Chalosse, Gascogne, Gers, Landes, Périgord and Quercy and guarantees that duck foie gras is raised, fattened and processed entirely within the South-West region.
quote: IGP Canard à Foie Gras du Sud-Ouest (covering Chalosse, Gascogne, Gers, Landes, Périgord, Quercy) ... ducks raised, fattened and cooked in the region

claim: Eugénie-les-Bains tourist office maps three signposted hiking loops from the town: Blue 3.3 km, Green 6.6 km, Red 7.2 km; plus Circuit de la Grave (8 km) and Circuit de la vallée du Bahus (15.1 km) from the former station.
quote: Blue Circuit: 3.3 km; Green Circuit: 6.6 km; Red Circuit: 7.2 km. Loop 3 (Circuit de la Grave): 8 km, starting from the former station near the bowling green. Loop 4 (Circuit de la vallée du Bahus): 15.1 km, same departure point.

claim: Aire-sur-l'Adour is a stage on the GR65 / Via Podiensis (Camino de Santiago Le Puy route), 26 km from Nogaro and 17 km onward to Miramont-Sensacq, passing the UNESCO-listed Church of Sainte Quitterie.
quote: From previous stage (Nogaro): 26 km. To next stage (Miramont-Sensacq): 17 km. The town's Church of Sainte Quitterie is UNESCO World Heritage-listed.

claim: The Scandibérique (EuroVelo 3) is a 1,776 km waymarked cycling route inaugurated in 2018 running from Maubeuge to Roncevaux through France, with stages crossing the Landes department.
quote: La Scandibérique, est 1 776 km long, connecting Maubeuge in the Nord to Roncevaux in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques. Inaugurated in June 2018.

claim: The official Scandibérique heads Mont-de-Marsan → Dax (33 km west), but a CycloTransEurope variant via Saint-Sever creates a Chalosse loop using the former railway greenway — Aire-sur-l'Adour is not on the marked main route.
quote: From Mont-de-Marsan, the official marked Scandibérique route heads west toward Dax to reach Tartas. CycloTransEurope proposes a variant by Saint-Sever that creates a loop through the slopes of Chalosse, an agricultural region crossed by a rustic greenway installed on the site of a former railway line.

claim: The Voie Verte de la Chalosse is a 34 km greenway on the former Saint-Sever–Dax railway, slightly undulating, passing Montfort, Montaut and Mugron through woods, hills and meadows.
quote: Length: 34 kilometres. Follows the old railway route linking Saint-Sever to the spa town of Dax. Towns: Saint-Sever, Montfort, Montaut, Mugron. The route offers rural and green landscapes featuring woods, hills and meadows.

claim: The Voie Verte de la Chalosse surface is not paved (stabilised gravel), unsuited to road bikes, with recommended departure points at Hinx and Saint-Sever (Augreilh district); the central Hauriet section closes during pigeon-hunting season.
quote: The path is not paved and not well-suited for road bikes. The recommended departure points are at Hinx and Saint-Sever (Augreilh district). The central section around the commune of Hauriet is closed during the pigeon hunting season.

claim: Canoë Kayak Aturin in Aire-sur-l'Adour (rue de la Violette) rents kayaks (€15/half-day, €25/day), double canoes (€30/€45) and paddleboards (€10/1h, €15/2h) June–early September, with descents up to 14 km along the Adour.
quote: Single kayak: €15 (half-day) / €25 (full day). Double canoe/kayak: €30 / €45. Paddleboard: €10 (1 hour) / €15 (2 hours). Season: June through early September. Trip Distance: Up to 14 km in nature along the river.

claim: Canoë Kayak Aturin runs daily in July–August (otherwise by appointment) with a 7 km loop from the nautical base taking about 2.5 hours; swimming ability required.
quote: Open from June 1, 2026. The facility offers departures from the nautical base with a 7km loop taking approximately 2.5 hours. Rental is available every day in July and August, and by appointment the rest of the year. Swimmers must know how to swim.

claim: Les Greens d'Eugénie (Golf du Tursan) at Bahus-Soubiran is a 9-hole par-35 course (2,786 m, slope 133/126) designed by Jean Larrouy in 1996, about 2 km from Eugénie-les-Bains, with vineyard-lined fairways and a stream crossing.
quote: Holes: 9. Par: 35. Distance: 2,786 meters. Slope Ratings: 133 (men), 126 (women). Designer: Jean Larrouy. Established: 1996. Located in Bahus-Soubiran approximately 2km from Eugénie-les-Bains.

claim: Les Greens d'Eugénie is open daily 9:00–18:30 year-round, with a 12-station practice (6 covered), putting green, equipment rental, lessons and a clubhouse with panoramic-terrace restaurant.
quote: Open daily 9:00 AM–6:30 PM (throughout 2026). The course includes 12 practice stations with 6 covered bays and a putting green. Additional amenities feature a clubhouse with bar service and dining options, including a panoramic terrace.

claim: Domaine de Benquet at Le Houga (8 km from Aire-sur-l'Adour, just over the Gers border) is a Cheval Qualité France-labelled equestrian centre offering pony baptisms from age 3, trail rides, vaulting and lessons, open daily.
quote: 3763 route de Benquet, 32460 Le Houga. 8Km d'Aire sur Adour, à droite. Baptême de poney dès 3 ans, balades et randonnées, voltige, travail à pied, attelage, cours d'équitation et stage. Cheval Qualité France accreditation. Open daily 9am-6pm (Monday-Saturday) and 2pm-6pm on Sundays.

claim: Saint-Sever Abbey is one of the 78 components of the UNESCO World Heritage 'Chemins de Compostelle en France' inscription, on the Voie de Vézelay (GR®654).
quote: Les chemins de Compostelle en France au Patrimoine mondial ... Voie de Vézelay (GR®654)

claim: The Saint-Sever abbey-church is freely accessible to visitors; standard adult guided-tour rate is in the €3–€5 range with self-guided exploration possible using tablets rented from the Tourist Office.
quote: Free admission during certain periods. Paid entry: €3–€5 for standard adult rates ... Visitors can explore independently or rent interpretive tablets from the Tourist Office for self-guided discovery.

claim: The Saint-Sever Beatus, produced at the abbey 1028–1072, is the only surviving illustrated Beatus commentary on the Apocalypse made north of the Pyrenees and inspired the fallen-soldier figure in Picasso's Guernica.
quote: the only surviving illustrated copy of Beatus of Liébana's commentary on the Apocalypse to have been produced north of the Pyrenees ... the figure of the fallen soldier is inspired by the huge figure of a drowned corpse in the illustration of the Great Flood in the Saint-Sever Beatus.

claim: The Samadet museum documents the local 18th-century earthenware manufactory tradition with three permanent rooms plus a temporary exhibition; demonstrations of faïence-making run the second Sunday of each month.
quote: The free museum visit includes the 3 permanent rooms and the temporary exhibition room ... Earthenware demonstrations occur on the second Sunday of each month from 3:30pm to 4:30pm.

claim: The Chapelle Notre-Dame des Cyclistes at Labastide-d'Armagnac is the national sanctuary of cycling, displaying jerseys of Poulidor, Merckx, Ocaña, Virenque and Jeannie Longo; open May 1 to October 15 (group tours year-round by reservation). Note: ~34 km from Eugénie, slightly beyond the 30 km radius.
quote: the Chapel of Cyclists houses a collection of champions' jerseys including those of Poulidor, Merckx, Ocaña, Virenque, and Jeanie Longo ... open from May 1 through October 15. Guided visits for groups of 20 people minimum are available year-round by reservation.

claim: The Collégiale Saint-Barthélemy de Pimbo (~14 km from Eugénie) is a 12th-century three-naved Romanesque church on the Camino de Santiago, with a richly carved portal of geometric semicircular arches; classified Monument Historique in 1998 and offering free visits.
quote: The collegiate church of Pimbo, situated on the route to Saint-James of Compostela, is first mentioned in an eleventh-century text. This 12th-century Romanesque edifice has three naves and three apses ... The entire collegiate church was classified as a historical monument in 1998.

claim: The Musée d'art et d'histoire du Cap de Gascogne (Jacobins convent, Saint-Sever) costs €4 full / €3 reduced (free under-10s), open Tue–Sun 14:30–18:30 in peak season with digital workshops devoted to the Gallo-Roman Gleyzia villa and the Beatus.
quote: Plein tarif : à partir de 4€ ; résidents de Saint-Sever, 10-18 ans, étudiants, demandeurs d'emploi : 3€ ; moins de 10 ans et titulaires Carte ICOM gratuit ... Du 1er juillet au 31 août 2025 : fermé lundi ; de mardi à dimanche de 14h30 à 18h30

claim: The Crypte de Saint-Girons at Hagetmau (~25 km from Eugénie) is a Greek-cross 11th–12th-century Romanesque jewel with 14 historiated capitals classified Monument Historique; open mid-June to mid-September 14:30–18:30 except Sundays, €3–4 (free under 10).
quote: The crypt is open from mid-June to mid-September from 2:30 PM to 6:30 PM except on Sundays ... 4 marble columns surround the slightly elevated ground where Saint Girons' tomb was located, and you can admire fourteen Romanesque capitals classified as Historic Monuments.

claim: Eugénie-les-Bains is ~15 km from Aire-sur-l'Adour, ~15 km from Grenade-sur-l'Adour, ~26 km from Mont-de-Marsan, and ~58 km from Pau; the A65 autoroute passes through Aire-sur-l'Adour with exits at both ends of town.
quote: Aire-sur-l'Adour approximately 15 km away... Grenade sur l'Adour about 15 km... Mont-de-Marsan 26 km from Eugénie-les-Bains... Pau Situated 58 km from Eugénie-les-Bains... A65 autoroute provides the fastest access, passing directly through Aire-sur-l'Adour

claim: Aire-sur-l'Adour to Eugénie-les-Bains is 13.5 km and ~17 minutes by road.
quote: Itinéraire AIRE SUR ADOUR EUGENIE LES BAINS 40. Distance 13,5 km dureé 17 minutes.

claim: Hagetmau to Eugénie-les-Bains is ~25.5 km, ~34 minutes by car — at the inner edge of a 30 km radius.
quote: Hagetmau to Eugénie-les-Bains: 34 minutes for a distance of 25.5 kilometers

claim: Samadet sits between Eugénie and Hagetmau (Hagetmau–Samadet is ~10 km, ~11 min), so Samadet from Eugénie is comfortably within the 30 km radius via D-roads.
quote: Hagetmau to Samadet: 10 km with an estimated driving time of 11 minutes

claim: Pau to Eugénie-les-Bains is ~68.9 km and ~55 minutes — outside the 30 km radius but reachable for a full day trip via A65.
quote: Itinéraire PAU 64 EUGENIE LES BAINS 40. Distance 68,9 km dureé 55 minutes.

claim: The Chapelle Notre-Dame des Cyclistes at Labastide-d'Armagnac is seasonally open 1 May–15 Oct, Tuesday–Sunday 15h–18h (closed Mondays), making it a spring/summer-only stop.
quote: open from May 1st to October 15th, Tuesday to Sunday from 3 PM to 6 PM

claim: The Écomusée de l'Armagnac at Château Garreau (3 km outside Labastide-d'Armagnac) combines a winegrower's museum, still museum, botanical trail and pond walks — a family-friendly half-day with an on-site escape game by reservation.
quote: Château Garreau extends over 82 hectares and houses the Écomusée de l'Armagnac... Winegrower's Museum (17th century), the Stills Museum (collection of more than 10 stills)... escape game is also available (by reservation), along with nature trails around the 6 ponds

claim: Hagetmau's Crypte de Saint-Girons (12th-c. capitals, Monument Historique) is open mid-June to mid-September, 14h30–18h30, closed Sundays — outside that window only by Tourism Office appointment.
quote: open from mid-June to mid-September from 2:30 PM to 6:30 PM except on Sundays. From May to October, contact the Tourism Office

claim: Pimbo, the oldest bastide of the Landes (founded 1268), is a free open-village stop on the Camino with a Romanesque collégiale — no ticketed hours, suitable any day including Sunday/Monday.
quote: Pimbo est la plus ancienne bastide des Landes fondée en 1268... important stopover sur la route de Saint-Jacques-de-Compostelle... la collégiale Saint-Barthélemy, une église romane

claim: The Château de Pau (Henri IV's birthplace) is open daily 9h30–11h45 & 14h–17h with no Monday closure, but closes 25 Dec, 1 Jan, and 1 May — usable as a full-day Sunday/Monday trip when Landes museums are shut.
quote: Le château est ouvert tous les jours de 9h30 à 11h45 et 14h à 17h... fermé les 25 décembre, 1er janvier et 1er mai. Il n'y a pas de fermeture systématique le lundi

claim: Family-friendly farm visits near Aire include a mini-farm of ~70 animals (rare ducks, Vietnamese pigs) run by an animateur trained for kids, plus 'La Forge animée' at Castelnau-Tursan — both viable substitutes for a proper zoo (the nearest, Zoo de Labenne, is on the Atlantic coast, well outside 30 km).
quote: Aire-sur-l'Adour, there is a mini-farm featuring 70 exceptional animals including birds, rare ducks, and Vietnamese pigs... 900 m² animal park... La Forge animée at Castelnau-Tursan
